quote: Das Dedekindsche Resultat lässt sich wahrscheinlich einfacher [-...-] durch Variation der Constanten beweisen, indem man zeigt, wie man von einem Systeme der $e_i$.. $l_i$[?] zu allen anderen durch continuirliche Verände- rung gelangen kann, ohne dass die Determi- nante $e = 0$ wird.
english: Dedekind's result can probably be proved more simply by variation of the constants, by showing how one can pass from one system of the e_i .. l_i to all others by continuous change without the determinant e becoming 0.
topic: Research notes proposing to generalise Dedekind's 1885 investigations on complex numbers (hypercomplex systems) to infinitely many units and to quaternions, and to reduce Sylvester's residue theorem, Cayley's intersection theorem and the Riemann-Roch theorem to relations between characteristic functions.

triage.modern_statement: The 'Dedekind result' here most likely means the Weierstrass (1884) and Dedekind (1885) theorem on commutative hypercomplex systems. In modern terms: a finite-dimensional commutative associative algebra over R (or C) with an identity whose discriminant (determinant) is nonzero, i.e. a semisimple algebra with no nilpotents, is isomorphic to a direct sum of copies of R and C (over C, to C^n). Hilbert proposes a deformation proof. Take the space of structure constants (the e_i … l_i) with nonzero determinant, show it is connected, so any system can be moved continuously to any other without the determinant becoming 0, and conclude that all such systems have the same structure. This is a proposal for a new proof of a known theorem, not a new conjecture.
triage.answered_by: The theorem itself was already proved by Weierstrass (Göttinger Nachrichten 1884) and Dedekind (Göttinger Nachrichten 1885, pp. 141–159; addendum 1887). Hilbert later published his own note under the same title, 'Zur Theorie der aus n Haupteinheiten gebildeten complexen Grössen' (Göttinger Nachrichten 1896, p. 179), which appears to carry out his idea of a simpler proof. I could not check whether that note actually uses the continuity / variation-of-constants argument. Today the result is a standard special case of the Wedderburn structure theory of semisimple commutative algebras.

Dedekind's 1885 reply to Weierstrass had the same title, and he added an 'Erläuterung' in 1887; history of the Weierstrass–Dedekind debate on hypercomplex numbers
In his 1885 and 1887 papers Dedekind writes hypercomplex numbers as finite sums Σ ξ_i e_i over 'principal units'

triage.why: The note proposes a simpler proof (a continuity/deformation argument) for a theorem Dedekind and Weierstrass had already proved; it is not an open problem. The classification of commutative semisimple algebras over R and C is fully settled and textbook material. Hilbert went on to publish a paper with exactly this title in the 1896 Göttinger Nachrichten, so he apparently took up the topic himself. My search budget ran out before I could confirm which method that paper uses, so I can't say whether his specific 'variation of the constants' proof was carried out there. That uncertainty is why confidence is medium. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem.
